title: Cybersecurity Benchmark Report 2026
description: Cybersecurity Benchmarks 2026: how security spending is growing, where organizations are focusing protections, and what buyers should evaluate in security platforms.
keyFindings: The cybersecurity segment shows 26% year-over-year growth in 2026
Enterprise adoption of cybersecurity solutions increased by 45% compared to last year
81% of organizations report improved outcomes after implementing cybersecurity software
Small and medium businesses account for 46% of cybersecurity software spending
AI-powered features are the top consideration for 63% of buyers evaluating cybersecurity platforms
Cloud-based deployment represents 76% of new cybersecurity software installations
Integration capabilities influence 79% of purchasing decisions
cybersecurity software budgets increased by an average of 28% in 2026

sections.title: The State of Security Spend
sections.body: Cybersecurity is the fastest-growing segment in our 2026 data at 26% year-over-year growth, and budgets rose by an average of 28%. The pattern reflects a shift from point defenses to platform consolidation: organizations are buying fewer, deeper products that cover more of the attack surface and share data across detection, response, and prevention.

sections.title: Adoption and Consolidation
sections.body: Enterprise adoption of cybersecurity solutions increased 45% compared to last year. Consolidation is the dominant theme: teams are retiring overlapping tools and standardizing on platforms with integrated detection and response. Organizations that consolidate report easier operations and faster investigation workflows than those maintaining many disconnected point products.

sections.title: Spending Patterns
sections.body: Small and medium businesses account for 46% of cybersecurity spending, reflecting how much of the market now sits below the enterprise tier. Budgets grew 28% on average in 2026, with the fastest increases in identity security and cloud security. Buyers should price platforms by endpoint and identity coverage rather than by feature count alone.

sections.title: What Buyers Evaluate
sections.body: AI-powered features are the top consideration for 63% of buyers evaluating security platforms, including automated threat detection, investigation assistance, and response recommendations. Integration capabilities influence 79% of purchasing decisions, because security tooling that cannot consume signals from the rest of the stack leaves gaps regardless of individual product quality.

sections.title: Regional Deployment Patterns
sections.body: Cloud-based deployment represents 76% of new security installations, lower than most other segments because some industries still require on-premise controls. Regulated sectors favor platforms with strong data-residency and audit features. Multi-region deployments are common for security platforms to cover globally distributed workforces.

sections.title: Recommendations
sections.body: Map the security controls you already own before comparing platforms, and identify which gaps overlap. Pilot one integrated platform on a defined attack scenario, measure detection and response times against the current baseline, and define the integration requirements early. Review the security stack quarterly, since the segment is evolving quickly.

methodology: This research is based on a survey of 1817 IT decision-makers, analysis of 178 software vendors, and secondary research from industry analysts. Data was collected in Q1-Q2 2026.
author: PilotStack Research Team
